Interface SlotGate

public interface SlotGate
What a slot accepts and releases, and how much of an item it holds: the value of BehaviorKeys.GATING, the slot author's rule. MenuKit resolves a gate for any slot, vanilla or created, by its Address and applies it once at each vanilla method that moves items: the slot's own mayPlace, mayPickup and getMaxStackSize (which every click, shift-click and automation path consults), the merge pass of moveItemStackTo, and the hopper and dispenser seams. A denied placement or pickup is refused before the mutation commits.

A gate is not a lock

A gate says what the slot is for: an elytra slot that takes only an elytra, a coin slot that holds one item. It belongs to whoever declared the slot. A lock is somebody else's policy laid over any slot ("nothing touches this one") and is a veto, never a gate. A veto can only say no and leaves the author's gate alone, so lifting the lock restores nothing.

The GatingContext

Each decision receives who is acting (GatingContext.actingPlayer), or null for automation, so a gate can answer per player.

    • maxStackSize

      default int maxStackSize(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, int vanillaMax)
      The per-item stack cap for this slot, given vanilla's own cap. The default imposes no extra limit; a gate that wants single-item slots returns Math.min(1, vanillaMax). The caller re-clamps to vanilla, so a gate can never raise the cap above what vanilla allows.
